page.text:
Functions are classified by how their mapping action behaves across the
domain and codomain:
- An *injective* (one-to-one) function preserves distinctness: no two
  distinct inputs share a common output. An injection embeds the domain
  into the codomain without loss of information.
- A *surjective* (onto) function covers the codomain entirely: every
  element in $B$ is realized as the output of at least one input in $A$.
- A *bijective* function is simultaneously injective and surjective. A
  bijection establishes an exact one-to-one correspondence between the
  sets $A$ and $B$, demonstrating that they possess identical cardinal
  size and abstract set-theoretic structure.
